workflows.title: Receipt/contract scan triage into tracker.csv
steps: Apply/update naming convention and log row in tracker.csv
workflows.trigger: A new scanned PDF (scan-0412.pdf .. scan-0423.pdf) appears, produced by an HP scanner set up via HP Easy Start / Printers & Scanners on 2026-10-15
workflows.outcome: tracker.csv accumulates one row per scan with extracted date/amount/type and a status/notes flag for exceptions, and the original PDF is renamed/moved on disk to the logged new_filename; by 2026-10-18T02:29:05Z it held 12 rows covering scans 0412-0423, with the last two (scan-0422, scan-0423) using a newly adopted TYPE_DATE_NAME.pdf naming convention instead of the earlier DATE_NAME_TYPE.pdf conve
variations: When the type is ambiguous, Morgan opens a separate client-types.txt reference file before logging the row (scan-0420, 2026-10-17T10:11:38Z-10:13:33Z)
Duplicate charges are cross-referenced against an already-logged row rather than filed normally (scan-0417)

From 2026-10-18, the proposed new_filename convention changed from DATE_NAME_TYPE.pdf to TYPE_DATE_NAME.pdf per naming-rule-update.txt (edited 2026-10-18T02:14:51-02:15:24Z); scan-0422 and scan-0423 are the first two rows logged under the new convention
limitations: HP printer driver setup (2026-10-15) is one-off configuration context, not part of the recurring triage procedure itself
No single ordered capture example covers every step of one occurrence end-to-end; procedure is reconstructed from multiple overlapping captures

The on-disk rename is now confirmed via Finder Date Modified correlation (18 Oct 2026 for the two newest files, matching session time) but the exact OS-level action (Save As, Finder rename, or script) was not directly observed in a capture
No ordered capture example covers every step. These references do not establish one end-to-end occurrence.
